words.ex: He speaks English with a French accent.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语时带有法国口音。
words.en: An accent is a distinctive way of pronouncing a language, especially one associated with a particular country, area, or social class.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.ex: The pollution affected the fish adversely.
words.ex_cn: 污染对鱼类造成了不利影响。
words.en: In a way that prevents success or development; harmfully or unfavorably.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.tr: adj. 确定的； v. 向…保证；“assure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was assured that the package would arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他确定包裹明天会到。
words.en: If you are assured of something, you are certain to get it or achieve it.

words.ex: Blood circulates in the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液在体内循环。
words.en: To move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area.

words.ex: The concept of freedom is important in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 自由这个观念在许多国家都很重要。
words.en: A concept is an idea or abstract principle.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.ex: He received criticism for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: Criticism is the act of expressing disapproval of someone or something and of the faults they have or the mistakes they have made.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: He dwells in a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一所小房子里。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: Her mother gave her encouragement before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 考试前，她妈妈给了她鼓励。
words.en: Encouragement is the act of giving someone support, confidence, or hope.

words.ex: She cheered enthusiastically for her team.
words.ex_cn: 她热情地为她的队伍加油。
words.en: If you do something enthusiastically, you do it with great eagerness and excitement.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.ex: He eats excessively sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多甜食。
words.en: To an excessive degree; more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; inordinately.

words.ex: He reads books as a hobby.
words.ex_cn: 他读书作为一种爱好。
words.en: A hobby is an activity that you enjoy doing in your spare time.

words.ex: His smile left a good impression on me.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑给我留下了好印象。
words.en: An idea, feeling, or opinion about something or someone, especially one formed without conscious thought or on the basis of little evidence.

words.ex: There was a big improvement in his English skills.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平有了很大改进。
words.en: The act of making something better or the state of being made better; an example or instance of this.

words.ex: The inadequacy of food caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 食物的不足导致了许多问题。
words.en: If there is an inadequacy in something, it is not enough or not good enough.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: He felt inferiority when he compared himself to his smarter brother.
words.ex_cn: 当他把自己和更聪明的哥哥比较时，他感到自己处于劣势。
words.en: The state of being lower in status or quality than another or others.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.tr: v. 做得过分；使…过度；过多使用
words.ex: Don't overdo the sugar in your tea.
words.ex_cn: 别在茶里放太多糖。
words.en: To do something to an excessive degree; to exaggerate or overuse something.

words.ex: He is overweight because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他超重是因为吃太多垃圾食品。
words.en: If someone is overweight, they weigh more than is considered healthy or attractive.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.ex: He gave a reasonable answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个合理的回答。
words.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive or extreme.

words.tr: v. 重新评价；再估价；使升值
words.ex: He will reevaluate his decision tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会重新评估他的决定。
words.en: If you reevaluate something or someone, you consider them again in order to reassess your opinion about them, especially if you think that your opinion should be changed.

words.ex: He felt sad after the rejection.
words.ex_cn: 在遭到拒绝后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The act of refusing to accept, believe in, or agree with something.

words.ex: He has high self-esteem after passing the test.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试后，他自尊心很强。
words.en: Self-esteem is the opinion you have of yourself and your abilities.

words.ex: His shyness made it hard to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他的害羞让他难以在全班面前说话。
words.en: Shyness is the feeling of being nervous or embarrassed in social situations, especially when meeting new people.

words.ex: The children laughed spontaneously when they saw the puppy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小狗时自发地笑了。
words.en: If something happens spontaneously, it happens without being planned or organized, or without any external influence.

words.ex: The company made a statement about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 公司就新政策发布了一项声明。
words.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way.

words.tr:
v. 旋动；（使）成漩涡；盘旋
n. 漩涡；涡状形
words.ex: The milk swirls in the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶在咖啡里旋转。
words.en: If something swirls or if you swirl it, it moves around and around quickly.

words.tr: adv. 若有所思地；沉思地；意味深长地；体贴地；关心地；
words.ex: He sat thoughtfully by the window, staring at the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他若有所思地坐在窗边，凝视着雨。
words.en: In a way that shows careful consideration or attention.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

words.ex: The old house looks unattractive with its peeling paint.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子油漆剥落，看起来没有魅力。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unattractive, you mean they are not pleasant to look at or do not have qualities that make them pleasant to be with.

words.tr: adj. 使人不舒服的；不自在的；
words.ex: The chair is uncomfortable to sit on.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子坐起来让人不舒服。
words.en: If you are uncomfortable, you are slightly worried or embarrassed, and not relaxed and confident.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；令人不安的；令人担忧的
words.ex: The dark clouds look worrisome.
words.ex_cn: 乌云看起来令人担忧。
words.en: If you describe something as worrisome, you mean that it causes you to feel anxious or concerned.

chapters.name: Unit 1 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 大量的，许多的（用于修饰可数名词复数）
words.ex: A great many students like to play soccer after school.
words.ex_cn: 非常多的学生喜欢放学后踢足球。
words.en: A large number of; very many.

words.tr: phrase. 许多，大量（用于修饰可数名词复数，相当于 many）
words.ex: A good many students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 很多学生通过了考试。
words.en: A large number of; many.

words.tr: phrase. 出现；跟随；进步；（催促）赶快
words.ex: I didn't see him, but he came along later.
words.ex_cn: 我没看到他，但他后来出现了。
words.en: To appear or arrive, often unexpectedly; to make progress or improve.

words.tr: phrase. v. 老是想着；过分关注（某事）； dwelling on 指反复思考或谈论不愉快的事
words.ex: He doesn't dwell on his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他不会纠结于自己的错误。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 手拉手地；紧密地；同时发生地
words.ex: They walk hand in hand in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们手拉手在公园里散步。
words.en: If two people are hand in hand, they are holding each other's hand. If two things go hand in hand, they are closely connected and one thing causes the other.

words.tr: phrase. 非常关心某事；把某事放在心上
words.ex: He has his family at heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把家人放在心上。
words.en: If you have something at heart, you are deeply concerned about it and it is very important to you.

words.ex: He likes cats. In contrast, she prefers dogs.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢猫。相比之下，她更喜欢狗。
words.en: used when you are comparing two things or people and saying that the second one is very different from the first

words.tr: phrase. 由某人自己选择的；某人选定的
words.ex: He picked a book of his choice from the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他从书架上选了一本自己想要的书。
words.en: Selected or preferred by a particular person or group.

words.tr: phrase. 放置一旁；留出；不理会；取消
words.ex: He sets aside $50 each week for savings.
words.ex_cn: 他每周存下50美元作为储蓄。
words.en: To reserve or keep something for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.ex: Please attach the file to the email.
words.ex_cn: 请将文件附加到邮件中。
words.en: To attach something to something else means to fasten or join it to the other thing.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.ex: He bought a brand-new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆全新的自行车。
words.en: Completely new, as if recently made or acquired.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: adj. 确信的；深信的；信服的； v. 说服；使确信；“convince”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I am convinced that he will win.
words.ex_cn: 我确信他会赢。
words.en: If you are convinced of something, you are sure that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr:
n. 饲料槽；有栏小卧床
v. 抄袭
words.ex: The horse eats hay from the crib.
words.ex_cn: 马从饲料槽里吃干草。
words.en: A crib is a bed with high sides for a baby or very young child. It can also mean to copy someone else's work and present it as your own.

words.ex: He lost his hearing and became deafness.
words.ex_cn: 他失去了听力，变成了耳聋。
words.en: Deafness is the condition of not being able to hear anything or not being able to hear very well.

words.tr:
n. 绝望；
v. 绝望；
words.ex: He felt despair after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到绝望。
words.en: Despair is the feeling that everything is wrong and that nothing will improve.

words.ex: There was a disagreement about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 关于这个计划，他们产生了分歧。
words.en: A disagreement is a situation in which people have different opinions about something and often argue.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.tr:
n. 离婚；
v. 和…离婚；
words.ex: They filed for divorce after ten years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚十年后申请了离婚。
words.en: Divorce is the formal ending of a marriage by law.

words.ex: The employer gave her a raise.
words.ex_cn: 雇主给她加了薪。
words.en: An employer is a person or organization that employs people, paying them for their work.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.ex: The furry cat curled up on the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 那只毛茸茸的猫蜷缩在沙发上。
words.en: Covered with or resembling fur.

words.ex: She wore a beautiful gown to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件漂亮的礼服去参加婚礼。
words.en: A gown is a long, loose piece of clothing worn on formal occasions or by people in particular professions.

words.ex: He habitually wakes up at 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯每天早上六点起床。
words.en: If someone does something habitually, they do it regularly or as a habit.

words.ex: He was sent to jail for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃被送进了监狱。
words.en: A place where people are kept as a punishment for a crime they have committed, or while they are waiting to go to court for their trial.

words.tr:
n. 叮当声；广告歌
v. （使）发出叮当声
words.ex: The bells make a happy jingle in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天里，铃铛发出愉快的叮当声。
words.en: A jingle is a short, simple tune, often with words, that is used to advertise a product or service on the radio or television.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.tr: adv. 与神经方面有关地
words.ex: The patient was examined neurologically to assess brain function.
words.ex_cn: 病人接受了神经方面的检查，以评估大脑功能。
words.en: In a manner relating to neurology or the nervous system.

words.ex: The newborn baby slept quietly in its mother's arms.
words.ex_cn: 新生的婴儿安静地躺在母亲的怀里。
words.en: A newborn baby or animal has recently been born.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.tr:
n. 溢出；
v. 泛滥；
words.ex: The rain caused an overflow of the river.
words.ex_cn: 雨水导致河水溢出。
words.en: If a liquid or a river overflows, it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.tr: n. 悲观主义者；悲观论者
words.ex: He is a pessimist who always expects the worst.
words.ex_cn: 他是个悲观者，总是预期最坏的结果。
words.en: A pessimist is someone who always expects that bad things will happen.

words.ex: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.tr: adj. 令人安心的； v. “reassure”的现在分词；
words.ex: Her smile was reassuring.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑令人安心。
words.en: If you find someone's words or actions reassuring, they make you feel less worried about something.

words.ex: The reversal of the decision made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的逆转让每个人都高兴。
words.en: A reversal is a change to an opposite direction, position, or course of action.

words.tr: adj. 自我应验的；自我实现的
words.ex: The prophecy became a self-fulfilling prophecy when people started to act as if it were true.
words.ex_cn: 当人们开始表现得好像预言是真的时，预言就变成了自我实现的预言。
words.en: A self-fulfilling prophecy or prediction is one that becomes true because people expect it to be true and behave in ways that make it happen.

words.ex: He had a setback when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，遇到了挫折。
words.en: A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

words.tr: adj. 无声的; 哑然无声
words.ex: The forest was soundless, save for the occasional rustling of leaves.
words.ex_cn: 森林里寂静无声，除了偶尔的树叶沙沙声。
words.en: If a place is soundless, it is completely quiet, with no sound at all.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: He arrived unusually early for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他开会时到得不平常地早。
words.en: To an unusual degree; exceptionally.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He is apt to forget his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他容易忘带钥匙。
words.en: Having a natural tendency; likely.

words.ex: He is prone to making small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他容易犯小错误。
words.en: If someone is prone to something, they are likely to do it or experience it.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 使高兴起来；振作起来
words.ex: He smiled to cheer up his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着让妹妹振作起来。
words.en: If someone cheers up, or if something cheers them up, they start to feel happier.

words.tr: phrase. 以…方式看待；从…角度理解；在…视角下
words.ex: He sees his teacher in a good light.
words.ex_cn: 他以良好的眼光看待他的老师。
words.en: In a particular way of considering or thinking about something.

words.tr: phrase. 受…控制；深陷于…之中；被…牢牢掌控
words.ex: The city was in the grip of a severe winter storm.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市正遭受一场严重的冬季风暴。
words.en: If someone or something is in the grip of a particular feeling or situation, they are being controlled or affected very strongly by it.

words.ex: He cooked dinner; meantime, the kids did their homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做晚饭；与此同时，孩子们在做作业。
words.en: The time between one event and another; meanwhile.

words.ex: He will run for mayor next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将竞选市长。
words.en: To compete for a position or office in an election.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.tr: n. 甜甜圈；油炸圈饼；炸面圈
words.ex: He ate a doughnut for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个甜甜圈。
words.en: A doughnut is a small, circular cake, usually with a hole in the middle, that is fried and often covered with sugar.

words.ex: He gave a dumb answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个愚笨的回答。
words.en: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak. If you describe someone or something as dumb, you mean that they are stupid or silly.

words.ex: The teacher gave an explanatory note to help students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个解释性的笔记来帮助学生。
words.en: Serving or intended to explain or make clear.

words.ex: The child was fearful of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子害怕黑暗。
words.en: If you are fearful of something, you are afraid of it.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr: n. 无依无靠；茫然若失；无可奈何的处境
words.ex: The old man felt helplessness after losing his family.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人在失去家人后感到无依无靠。
words.en: The state of being unable to help oneself; the feeling or condition of being powerless or unable to act.

words.ex: He felt hopelessness after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到绝望。
words.en: The feeling or state of despair; lack of hope.

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.tr: adj. 无能力的；不称职的；不能胜任的；
words.ex: He is incompetent at managing simple tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他无法胜任简单的任务。
words.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.tr: v. 预防注射；接种疫苗
words.ex: The doctor will inoculate the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To inoculate someone against a disease means to inject a weak form of the disease into their body as a way of protecting them against it.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.ex: His performance in the game was excellent.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的表现非常出色。
words.en: The act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment.

words.ex: His pessimism made him expect the worst.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲观主义让他总是预期最坏的结果。
words.en: Pessimism is the belief that bad things are going to happen or that something is going to turn out badly.

words.tr:
n. 代表；典型事物；
adj. 典型的；有代表性的；代议制的；
words.ex: He is the representative of our class.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们班的代表。
words.en: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.ex: He watched the whole series of the show.
words.ex_cn: 他看完了这部剧的整个系列。
words.en: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other.

words.ex: He tied his shoelace before running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步前系好了鞋带。
words.en: A shoelace is a cord or strip of leather used to fasten a shoe.

words.ex: He is a deep thinker who solves problems slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个深思熟虑的思考者，慢慢解决问题。
words.en: A thinker is someone who spends a lot of time thinking deeply about important things, especially someone who is famous for thinking of new or interesting ideas.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrasal verb. 阻碍某人；阻止某人前进；抑制某人
words.ex: Fear can hold someone back from trying new things.
words.ex_cn: 恐惧会阻碍人们尝试新事物。
words.en: To prevent someone from making progress or developing.

words.tr: phrase. 处于某种情绪（或心情）之中
words.ex: She is in a happy mood today.
words.ex_cn: 她今天心情愉快。
words.en: Feeling or displaying a particular emotion or state of mind.

words.tr: phrase. 在某种程度上；部分地
words.ex: He succeeded in part because he worked hard.
words.ex_cn: 他部分成功是因为他努力工作。
words.en: To some extent; not completely.

words.ex: I keep track of my expenses every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天记录我的开支。
words.en: To keep track of something means to stay informed about it or to record it, especially in order to notice any changes or developments.

words.tr: phrase. 伸手去抓；努力争取；寻求（帮助、支持等）
words.ex: The child reaches out for the toy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子伸手去拿玩具。
words.en: To extend one's hand in an attempt to grab or touch something; to seek help or support from someone.

words.tr: phrase. 居功；把功劳归于自己
words.ex: He likes to take credit for other people's work.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把别人的功劳归于自己。
words.en: To claim or accept praise, recognition, or responsibility for something, especially when it may not be entirely deserved.

words.ex: The teacher gave her approval for the project.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这个项目表示了赞成。
words.en: If you give your approval to something, you agree with it or allow it to happen.

words.tr:
n. 大炮；火炮
v. 猛撞；碰撞
words.ex: The soldiers fired the cannon at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们向敌人开炮。
words.en: A cannon is a large, heavy piece of artillery which was used in wars to fire heavy metal balls or shells.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.tr: adv. 忠实地；尽职地；顺从地
words.ex: He dutifully does his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都认真地做作业。
words.en: If you say that someone does something dutifully, you mean that they do it because they have been told to or because they feel it is their duty.

words.tr:
n. 染料；
v. 给...染色；
words.ex: She bought a natural dye to color her fabric.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一种天然染料来给布料染色。
words.en: A dye is a substance used to change the color of something permanently. To dye something means to change its color by applying a dye.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The children built a hut in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树林里建了一间小屋。
words.en: A hut is a small, simple building, usually consisting of one room and made of materials such as wood, mud, or grass.

words.ex: He received an invitation to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了参加派对的邀请。
words.en: An invitation is a written or spoken request to come to an event such as a party, a meal, or a meeting.

words.tr:
n. 痒；渴望
v. （使）痒；渴望
words.ex: The mosquito bite caused an itchy on my arm.
words.ex_cn: 蚊子叮咬让我的手臂发痒。
words.en: If you have an itch, you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch. If you itch to do something, you are very eager or impatient to do it.

words.ex: He put a mat on the floor to keep it clean.
words.ex_cn: 他在地上放了一块垫子以保持清洁。
words.en: A mat is a piece of thick fabric or other material that is placed on a floor or other surface to protect it or to provide a soft surface to stand or sit on.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；淘气；伤害；损害
words.ex: The boy caused mischief by letting the cats out.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩放出了猫，惹了麻烦。
words.en: Mischief is behavior, especially by children, that is slightly bad but is not intended to cause serious harm or damage.

words.tr: adj. 调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
words.ex: The mischievous boy laughed and hid his sister's shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩笑着藏起了他姐姐的鞋子。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as mischievous, you mean that they enjoy playing tricks on people or doing things to annoy or embarrass them.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.tr: n. 演说者；演讲者；雄辩家；
words.ex: He is a famous orator who speaks at large events.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在大型活动中演讲的著名演说者。
words.en: An orator is a person who delivers speeches or lectures, especially one who is skilled at doing so.

words.ex: The palm tree grows near the beach.
words.ex_cn: 棕榈树长在海滩附近。
words.en: The inner surface of the hand that extends from the wrist to the base of the fingers; also refers to the tropical tree with large divided leaves.

words.ex: The parrot can say hello.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹦鹉会说你好。
words.en: A parrot is a tropical bird with a curved beak and brightly colored feathers. Parrots are often kept as pets because they can be taught to copy human speech.

words.tr:
v. 啄；连续敲击；轻吻
n. 啄痕；啄食；轻吻
words.ex: The bird pecked at the bread on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿啄地上的面包。
words.en: To peck means to strike or bite something with the beak, or to kiss someone lightly and quickly.

words.ex: The bird's plumage was a vibrant mix of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟的羽毛色彩鲜艳。
words.en: The feathers covering the body of a bird.

words.tr:
n. 拨浪鼓；嘎嘎声；咔嗒声
v. 发出格格声；使紧张不安；喋喋不休
words.ex: The baby laughed while shaking the rattle.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝摇着拨浪鼓笑了。
words.en: If something rattles or if you rattle it, it makes short sharp knocking sounds as it moves or shakes.

words.tr:
n. 壳体；贝壳；炮弹；
v. 剥…的壳；去…的皮；炮轰；炮击；
words.ex: The crab crawled out of its shell.
words.ex_cn: 螃蟹从它的壳里爬了出来。
words.en: A shell is the hard protective outer case of a mollusk or crustacean, or the outer layer of an egg, nut, or seed. It can also refer to a metal case filled with explosive, to be fired from a gun.

words.tr: adj. 有技巧的；熟练的；灵巧的；
words.ex: He is a skillful painter who draws beautiful landscapes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有技巧的画家，能画出美丽的风景。
words.en: Someone who is skillful at something does it very well.

words.ex: He gave a sniff of the flower.
words.ex_cn: 他闻了闻那朵花。
words.en: To sniff is to breathe in air through your nose in a way that makes a noise, especially when you are trying to smell something or when you have a cold.

words.ex: I am somewhat tired after work.
words.ex_cn: 下班后我有点累。
words.en: You use somewhat to indicate that something is the case to a limited extent or degree.

words.ex: The warrior threw a spear at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 战士向敌人投掷了一支矛。
words.en: A spear is a weapon consisting of a long pole with a sharp point at one end, used for thrusting or throwing.

words.ex: The spokesman spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokesman is a man who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization.

words.ex: The old man is a good storyteller.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是个出色的故事讲述者。
words.en: A storyteller is someone who tells or writes stories.

words.ex: The tortoise moves slowly across the grass.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟慢慢地在草地上爬行。
words.en: A tortoise is a slow-moving land animal with a shell into which it can pull its head and legs for protection.

words.tr: adj. 不领情的；忘恩负义的
words.ex: He was ungrateful for the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他对这份礼物毫不感激。
words.en: If you describe someone as ungrateful, you are criticizing them for not showing thanks or for being unkind to someone who has helped them or done them a favour.

words.ex: He cooked a yam for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他为晚餐煮了一个薯蓣。
words.en: A yam is a root vegetable that is similar to a sweet potato and is often used in cooking.

chapters.name: Unit 2 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: 短语. 一想到……就……，表示因想到某事而产生某种情绪或反应
words.ex: She shuddered at the thought of going back there.
words.ex_cn: 一想到要回到那里，她就不寒而栗。
words.en: Upon thinking about or considering something, often leading to a reaction.

words.tr: 短语. 一想到……就……，表示因想到某事而立即产生某种情绪或反应
words.ex: She shivered at the very thought of going into the dark basement.
words.ex_cn: 一想到要走进黑暗的地下室，她就颤抖。
words.en: Immediately upon thinking about something, often used to express a strong emotional reaction to the idea.

words.ex: He choose to walk to school instead of taking the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他选择走路去学校，而不是坐公交车。
words.en: to decide to do something, especially when you have a choice

words.tr: 短语动词. 未被某人注意到；逃过某人的察觉
words.ex: The mistake escaped her notice.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误她没有注意到。
words.en: If something escapes someone's notice, they do not see it or realize it.

words.tr: phrase. 突然站起来；一跃而起
words.ex: When the fire alarm rang, he jumped to his feet and ran to the door.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，他立刻跳起来跑向门口。
words.en: To stand up quickly, especially in response to a sudden stimulus or surprise.

words.ex: We go to the cinema now and again.
words.ex_cn: 我们偶尔会去看电影。
words.en: Occasionally; from time to time.

words.tr: phrase. 放心；确信无疑；尽管放心
words.ex: Rest assured, I will help you with your homework.
words.ex_cn: 放心吧，我会帮你做作业。
words.en: If you say that someone can rest assured that something is the case, you mean that it is definitely the case, so they do not need to worry about it.

words.tr: phrase. 出发；动身；使爆炸；引起
words.ex: He set off early to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他早早出发以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: To begin a journey or to cause something to start or happen.

words.tr: phrase. 缓慢但稳妥地；稳扎稳打地
words.ex: He is slowly but surely learning to speak English.
words.ex_cn: 他正在一点一点地学会说英语。
words.en: Gradually and steadily, making progress despite the slow pace.

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.tr: int. 哎呀！ （表示悲伤、恐惧）；
words.ex: Alas, the little dog was lost in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 哎呀，小狗在风暴中走丢了。
words.en: used to express sadness or disappointment

words.tr:
adj. 恼怒的；气恼的
v. 使恼怒；使气恼；“annoy”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is annoyed by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 他被吵闹的声音惹恼了。
words.en: If you are annoyed, you are fairly angry about something.

words.tr: adj. 感激的；欣赏的；表示赞赏的
words.ex: She was appreciative of his help.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的帮助心怀感激。
words.en: If you are appreciative of something, you are grateful for it.

words.tr: v. 使惊讶；“astonish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was astonished by the sudden news.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个突然的消息惊呆了。
words.en: If you are astonished by something, you are very surprised about it.

words.ex: The king banish the traitor from the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 国王将叛徒驱逐出王国。
words.en: To banish someone means to send them away from a country or place and not allow them to return.

words.ex: The beast ran fast through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 那只野兽在森林里快速奔跑。
words.en: A beast is a large and dangerous animal.

words.ex: She gave a cheerful smile.
words.ex_cn: 她露出了快乐的微笑。
words.en: Someone who is cheerful is happy and shows this in their behavior.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: He didn't study, consequently he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有学习，因此考试不及格。
words.en: As a result; therefore.

words.tr: n. （名词）畸形状态：遭致变形后的状态
words.ex: The accident caused a deformity in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 事故导致他的腿变形。
words.en: A deformity is a part of someone's body that is not the normal shape because of injury, illness, or because they were born that way.

words.ex: The departure of the train was at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 火车的出发时间是晚上8点。
words.en: The act of leaving a place, especially at the start of a journey.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.tr: adj. 空手的；一无所获的
words.ex: He returned home empty-handed after a long day of searching.
words.ex_cn: 经过一整天的寻找，他空手而归。
words.en: If you come away from a place empty-handed, you have failed to obtain what you wanted.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the pigs to fatten them.
words.ex_cn: 农夫喂猪使它们长胖。
words.en: To make or become fat or fatter.

words.ex: He sits by the fireplace in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天他坐在壁炉旁。
words.en: A fireplace is a place built into a wall where you can have a fire, especially in a house.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.tr: adj. 脾气好的；温厚的；和蔼的
words.ex: She was always good-natured and willing to help.
words.ex_cn: 她总是很和善，乐于助人。
words.en: A good-natured person is friendly and does not easily get angry.

words.tr: v. 同意；赞成；“agree”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 已一致的；同意的；
words.ex: We agreed to meet at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我们同意下午五点见面。
words.en: If people are agreed, they have reached a joint decision on something or have the same opinion about something.

words.ex: He felt deep grief after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到深深的悲痛。
words.en: Intense sorrow, especially caused by someone's death.

words.ex: She was grief-stricken after losing her husband.
words.ex_cn: 失去丈夫后，她极度悲伤。
words.en: Overwhelmed by or suffering from grief.

words.ex: The ship docked at the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbor is a place on the coast where ships may moor in shelter, especially one protected from rough water by piers, jetties, and other artificial structures.

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.ex: The movie was horrible and made me scared.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很恐怖，让我害怕。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as horrible, you mean they are very unpleasant or bad.

words.ex: The wolf howl at the moon.
words.ex_cn: 狼对着月亮嚎叫。
words.en: If a dog or wolf howls, it makes a long, loud, crying sound. If a person howls, they make a long, loud cry expressing pain, anger, or unhappiness.

words.tr:
v. 拥抱；紧抱；抱有；挨着
n. 拥抱；搂抱
words.ex: She gave him a big hug when he arrived.
words.ex_cn: 他到达时，她给了他一个大大的拥抱。
words.en: To hug someone means to put your arms around them and hold them tightly, for example because you like them or are pleased to see them.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.ex: The magnificence of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的壮丽让每个人都很惊讶。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.tr: n. 女主人；情妇；女教师（英）
words.ex: The mistress of the house welcomed the guests warmly.
words.ex_cn: 女主人热情地欢迎了客人。
words.en: A woman who has control or authority over others, especially a woman who is in charge of a household or institution.

words.ex: The old ship was a monster on the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在海上是个庞然大物。
words.en: A monster is an imaginary creature that is very large, ugly, and frightening.

words.ex: The child showed obedience to his parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对父母表现出顺从。
words.en: Obedience is the act of following orders or instructions from someone in authority.

words.ex: He chopped an onion for the soup.
words.ex_cn: 他为汤切了一个洋葱。
words.en: An onion is a round vegetable with a light brown skin. It has many layers and a strong, sharp smell and taste.

words.tr:
adj. 充满喜悦的；大喜的
v. 使大喜；“overjoy”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She was overjoyed when she got the gift.
words.ex_cn: 她收到礼物时欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are overjoyed, you are extremely happy about something.

words.ex: His presence made everyone feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他的存在让每个人都感到平静。
words.en: The state or fact of existing, occurring, or being present in a place or thing.

words.ex: The prince rode a white horse through the castle gate.
words.ex_cn: 王子骑着一匹白马穿过城堡的大门。
words.en: A prince is a male member of a royal family, especially the son of a king or queen.

words.tr:
v. 吼叫；咆哮
n. 吼叫；咆哮
words.ex: The lion let out a loud roar.
words.ex_cn: 狮子发出了一声响亮的咆哮。
words.en: If something roars, it makes a very loud noise, like the sound of a lion.

words.ex: She planted a rosebush in her garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里种了一丛玫瑰。
words.en: A rosebush is a bush that produces roses.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The wizard waved his wand and made the ball disappear.
words.ex_cn: 巫师挥动他的魔杖，让球消失了。
words.en: A wand is a thin, straight stick that is used by magicians to perform magic tricks or by conductors to direct an orchestra.

words.ex: The wicked witch cast a spell on the prince.
words.ex_cn: 邪恶的女巫对王子施了咒语。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as wicked, you mean that they are very bad, immoral, or cruel.

words.tr:
v. 转换；
n. 开关；
words.ex: He switched off the light before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前把灯关掉了。
words.en: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 充满…的；被…所占据的（通常指情绪或激情，如愤怒、焦虑、热情等）
words.ex: She was consumed with jealousy after learning about his new relationship.
words.ex_cn: 得知他的新恋情后，她被嫉妒所吞噬。
words.en: If you are consumed with a feeling or idea, it affects you very strongly indeed.

words.tr: verb phrase. 被……所吞噬；被……完全占据（常指情绪或激情）
words.ex: She was consumed by guilt after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，她被内疚感所吞噬。
words.en: To be completely absorbed or preoccupied by a particular feeling, thought, or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 对……施加魔法；迷住，使着迷
words.ex: The witch cast a spell on the prince, turning him into a frog.
words.ex_cn: 女巫对王子施了魔法，将他变成了一只青蛙。
words.en: To use magic to affect someone or something, often in a way that changes their behavior or appearance.

words.tr: phrase. 对……施加魔力；迷住，使着迷
words.ex: Her beauty cast a spell over everyone who met her.
words.ex_cn: 她的美貌让每个见到她的人都为之着迷。
words.en: To cast a spell over someone or something means to use magic to affect them, or to captivate or enchant them in a way that seems magical.

words.ex: He used honey in place of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他用蜂蜜代替了糖。
words.en: Instead of someone or something else.

words.tr: phrase. 使某事终止；结束某事；制止某事
words.ex: The new rules will put an end to cheating in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 新规则将杜绝考试作弊。
words.en: To cause something to stop or finish.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: The alchemist tried to turn lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 炼金术士试图把铅变成黄金。
words.en: An alchemist is a person who studies or practices alchemy, which was a form of chemistry and speculative philosophy practiced in the Middle Ages and the Renaissance, concerned principally with discovering methods for transmuting baser metals into gold and with finding a universal solvent and an elixir of life.

words.ex: The priest placed the offering on the altar.
words.ex_cn: 牧师把供品放在祭坛上。
words.en: An altar is a raised area in a place of worship where people can honor God with offerings.

words.ex: The sailors swam ashore after the boat sank.
words.ex_cn: 船沉没后，水手们游到了岸上。
words.en: If someone or something comes ashore, they come from the sea onto the shore.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.ex: He uses a facial cleanser every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上使用洁面乳。
words.en: A cleanser is a substance that you use to clean your skin or to clean objects.

words.ex: The committee meets every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会每周一开会。
words.en: A committee is a group of people who are chosen to do a particular job or make decisions on behalf of a larger group.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: The boy drew a big dragon on his notebook.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在他的笔记本上画了一条大龙。
words.en: A mythical monster like a giant reptile. In European tradition, it is typically fire-breathing and tends to symbolize chaos or evil, whereas in East Asia it is usually a beneficent symbol of fertility, associated with water and the heavens.

words.ex: The emperor ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位皇帝统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A male sovereign ruler of an empire.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；有见识的；启迪的
v. 启发；开导；“enlighten”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is an enlightened teacher who helps students think clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，帮助学生清晰思考。
words.en: If you describe someone or their attitudes as enlightened, you mean that they have sensible, modern attitudes and ways of dealing with things.

words.ex: The town holds a music festival every summer.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇每年夏天都举办音乐节。
words.en: A festival is an organized series of events such as musical concerts or drama productions, often happening annually in the same place.

words.ex: He worked hard to fulfill his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的梦想。
words.en: To fulfill a task, role, or function means to do or perform it as required or expected.

words.ex: The blacksmith heated the metal in the furnace.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠在熔炉里加热金属。
words.en: A furnace is a device that produces heat for warmth or to melt materials.

words.ex: She dresses like a goddess on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 她在万圣节打扮得像一位女神。
words.en: A goddess is a female deity. In many cultures, goddesses are associated with Earth, motherhood, love, and the household.

words.ex: The governor signed the new law yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 州长昨天签署了这项新法律。
words.en: A governor is a person who is responsible for the political administration of a region, such as a state or a colony.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr:
int. 喂；哈喽；
n. “喂”的招呼声或问候声；
words.ex: Hello, can you hear me?
words.ex_cn: 喂，你能听到我吗？
words.en: used as a greeting or to begin a telephone conversation

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.ex: Some people believe in immortality after death.
words.ex_cn: 有些人相信死后会有永生。
words.en: The state of being able to live or last forever.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 不负责任的；无责任感的；
words.ex: He is irresponsible because he never pays his bills.
words.ex_cn: 他从不付账单，所以是不负责任的。
words.en: If you describe someone as irresponsible, you are criticizing them because they do things without properly considering their possible consequences.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.ex: His judgment was clear and fair.
words.ex_cn: 他的判断清晰而公正。
words.en: A judgment is an opinion that you have or express after thinking carefully about something.

words.ex: The lion is the king of the animal kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是动物王国之王。
words.en: A kingdom is a country or region that is ruled by a king or queen.

words.tr:
n. 跳跃；
v. 跳跃；
words.ex: The cat made a big leap over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 猫跳过了篱笆。
words.en: To leap means to jump high or a long way, or to move quickly and with a lot of energy.

words.ex: He put the lid on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他把盖子盖在盒子上。
words.en: A lid is a cover for a container, or the movable cover of the eye, known as the eyelid.

words.tr:
n. 魔术；魔法；
adj. 魔术（似）的；神奇的；
words.ex: He performed magic at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上表演了魔术。
words.en: Magic is the power to use supernatural forces to make impossible things happen, such as making people disappear or controlling events in nature.

words.tr: v. 行为不端；行为无礼貌
words.ex: The boy misbehaved in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上行为不端。
words.en: If someone, especially a child, misbehaves, they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.ex: He ate a ripe peach for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个熟透的桃子。
words.en: A peach is a soft, round, slightly furry fruit with sweet yellow flesh and pinky-orange skin. Peaches grow in warm countries.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.tr: n. 朝圣之旅；参拜之行；瞻仰之旅；
words.ex: Many people go on a pilgrimage to the holy city.
words.ex_cn: 许多人前往圣城进行朝圣之旅。
words.en: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place for religious reasons.

words.tr:
v. 撒尿
n. 小便
words.ex: He went outside to take a piss.
words.ex_cn: 他出去小便。
words.en: To urinate; to pass liquid waste from the body.

words.tr: adv. 异常地，惊人地，巨大地
words.ex: He worked prodigiously hard to achieve his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他异常努力地工作以实现他的目标。
words.en: In a way that is remarkably or impressively great in extent, size, or degree.

words.ex: The math teacher asked for a proof of the theorem.
words.ex_cn: 数学老师要求给出这个定理的证明。
words.en: Proof is a fact, argument, or piece of evidence which shows that something is definitely true or definitely exists.

words.ex: Saint Francis loved animals and helped the poor.
words.ex_cn: 圣方济各热爱动物并帮助穷人。
words.en: A saint is a person who is recognized as having an exceptional degree of holiness, likeness, or closeness to God.

words.ex: He reads scripture every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读经文。
words.en: The sacred writings of a religion; often used to refer to the Bible.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: The bridge is stable and safe to cross.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥很稳固，可以安全通过。
words.en: If something is stable, it is not likely to change or come to an end suddenly.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.ex: He felt victorious after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到胜利。
words.en: Having won a victory; conquering.

words.tr:
n. 誓言；誓约
v. 发誓；起誓
words.ex: He made a vow to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓戒烟。
words.en: A vow is a serious promise or decision to do something.

words.ex: He found a weapon in the old box.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧箱子里发现了一件武器。
words.en: A weapon is an object that can be used to harm or kill someone, or to damage or destroy something.

words.ex: The wickedness of the crime shocked the community.
words.ex_cn: 这起罪行的邪恶性震惊了整个社区。
words.en: Wickedness is the quality of being wicked, which means morally very bad and deliberately intending to harm people.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: phrase. 随心所欲地；随意地
words.ex: He can leave at will.
words.ex_cn: 他可以随时离开。
words.en: If you can do something at will, you can do it when you want and in the way that you want.

words.ex: He greet his friend with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着向朋友问好。
words.en: To greet someone means to say hello to them or to welcome them.

words.ex: When I arrived at the party, I was greeted by a warm smile from the host.
words.ex_cn: 当我到达派对时，主人用一个温暖的微笑迎接我。
words.en: To be met or encountered by someone or something in a particular way.

words.ex: The teacher asked the children to behave themselves during the trip.
words.ex_cn: 老师要求孩子们在旅行期间要守规矩。
words.en: To conduct oneself in a specified way, especially in a way that is socially acceptable.

words.tr: phrase. 判处某人死刑；将某人定罪并判处死刑
words.ex: The judge will condemn the man to death.
words.ex_cn: 法官将判处那个人死刑。
words.en: To officially decide that someone must be punished by death, especially by a legal process.

words.ex: He must conform to the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他必须遵守校规。
words.en: To comply with rules, standards, or laws; to behave according to socially acceptable conventions or standards.

words.ex: He will hand over the keys tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会交出钥匙。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially because you have been ordered to do so or because it is necessary.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 将某人交给当局或对方；移交某人
words.ex: The police will hand the suspect over to the court.
words.ex_cn: 警方将把嫌疑人移交给法院。
words.en: To deliver someone to the custody or control of another, especially the authorities.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 把某物交出；移交；让出
words.ex: Please hand the book over to me.
words.ex_cn: 请把书交给我。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially after being asked or told to do so.

words.tr: phrase. 自愿地；主动地；自发地
words.ex: He cleaned his room of his own accord.
words.ex_cn: 他主动打扫了自己的房间。
words.en: If you do something of your own accord, you do it because you want to, without being asked or forced.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人报仇；对某人进行报复
words.ex: He wants to take revenge on someone who stole his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想向偷他自行车的人报仇。
words.en: To harm someone because they have harmed you.

words.tr: phrase. 肯定地；确凿无疑地
words.ex: He knows with certainty that the train will arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 他确信火车会准时到达。
words.en: With absolute confidence or without doubt.

words.ex: The new park has better accessibility for wheelchair users.
words.ex_cn: 这个新公园为轮椅使用者提供了更好的可及性。
words.en: The quality of being able to be reached or entered.

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 运动的；身强力壮的；
words.ex: He is an athletic boy who loves running.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱跑步的运动型男孩。
words.en: Athletic is used to describe someone who is physically strong, fit, and good at sports, or something related to sports or physical activities.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: She spoke candidly about her experiences.
words.ex_cn: 她坦率地谈论了她的经历。
words.en: In a straightforward and honest way.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: He likes coffee; conversely, she prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡；相反，她更喜欢茶。
words.en: In a way that is the opposite or reverse of something else.

words.ex: We usually have dinner at dinnertime.
words.ex_cn: 我们通常在正餐时间吃晚餐。
words.en: The time at which dinner is usually eaten.

words.tr: adj. 令人失望的；令人扫兴的； v. “disappoint”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影令人失望。
words.en: If something is disappointing, it is not as good as you hoped it would be.

words.ex: He dozed off during the boring meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的会议上打起了瞌睡。
words.en: To doze means to sleep lightly or for a short period.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: The new tool enables him to finish work faster.
words.ex_cn: 这个新工具使他能够更快地完成工作。
words.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity or means to do it.

words.ex: The expense of the trip was higher than expected.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行的费用比预期的要高。
words.en: An expense is the amount of money that you spend on something.

words.ex: He paid the fee to join the club.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了加入俱乐部的费用。
words.en: A fee is a sum of money that you pay to be allowed to do something such as join an organization, or to be given advice or a service.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.tr: adj. 引起恐惧的；使惊恐的；骇人的； v. “frighten”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark forest looked frightening at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来很吓人。
words.en: If you say that something is frightening, you mean that it makes you feel afraid or anxious.

words.ex: He feels fulfillment when he helps others.
words.ex_cn: 当他帮助别人时，他感到满足。
words.en: Fulfillment is the feeling of being happy and satisfied because you are doing something useful or important, or because you have achieved something.

words.ex: He likes reading, and furthermore, he writes stories too.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢阅读，而且他还写故事。
words.en: In addition to what has been said; moreover.

words.ex: She is a homemaker who takes care of her children.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位照顾孩子的家庭主妇。
words.en: A homemaker is a person, especially a housewife, who manages a home.

words.tr: n. 住房供给； v. 收容；“house”的现在分词；
words.ex: The city needs more housing for low-income families.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要为低收入家庭提供更多的住房供给。
words.en: Housing refers to buildings or other shelters in which people live; a place to live.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.ex: He felt isolation after moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他搬到新城市后感到孤立。
words.en: The state of being in a place or situation that is separate from others

words.tr: n. 闩锁钥匙，弹簧锁钥匙
words.ex: She always carried a latchkey in case she came home late.
words.ex_cn: 她总是随身携带一把弹簧锁钥匙，以防回家晚了。
words.en: A latchkey is a key to an outside door of a house or apartment, especially one that is carried by a child who lets themselves into the house after school.

words.ex: He showed maturity when he apologized for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他为自己的错误道歉时，表现出了成熟。
words.en: Maturity is the state of being fully developed or grown, or the time when a financial arrangement becomes ready to be paid.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The rainbow is a natural phenomenon.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹是一种自然现象。
words.en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist, especially something that is unusual or interesting.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.ex: He felt resentful when his friend got the promotion.
words.ex_cn: 当他朋友得到晋升时，他感到怨恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing bitterness or indignation about having been treated unfairly.

words.ex: He felt resentment after being ignored by his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他被朋友忽视后感到怨恨。
words.en: Resentment is a feeling of anger or bitterness about something that you believe is unfair.

words.ex: He is a salaried employee with a fixed monthly income.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名领薪水的雇员，有固定的月收入。
words.en: Receiving a salary; employed for a salary.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: The temperature rose steadily throughout the day.
words.ex_cn: 白天温度稳定地上升。
words.en: If something happens or changes steadily, it happens or changes in a regular way without interruption.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: The tuition for this course is $500.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程的学费是500美元。
words.en: Tuition is the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college, university, or private school.

words.ex: The diary helped unlock the mystery of her disappearance.
words.ex_cn: 这本日记帮助揭开了她失踪的谜团。
words.en: To unlock something means to open it, or to make it possible for someone to open it, by turning a key or pushing a button.

words.tr: adj. 无人监督的；无人管理的；
words.ex: The children played in the park in an unsupervised way.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在无人监督的情况下在公园里玩耍。
words.en: Not watched or managed by someone in authority.

words.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
words.ex_cn: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。
words.en: If you describe a situation or a feeling as a void, you mean that it seems empty because there is nothing interesting or worthwhile about it.

words.tr: adj. 流传甚广的；分布广的；
words.ex: The flu became widespread last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感流传甚广。
words.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

chapters.name: Unit 3 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He didn't win, but after all, he tried his best.
words.ex_cn: 他没有赢，但毕竟他尽了最大努力。
words.en: You use after all when you are saying that something that you thought might not be the case is in fact the case.

words.tr: phrase. 太常；屡次发生地；不幸的是经常
words.ex: He misses the bus all too often.
words.ex_cn: 他经常错过公交车。
words.en: Used to say that something happens more often than it should, usually something bad.

words.ex: He tries to cope with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To deal effectively with something difficult.

words.ex: He started to doze off during the boring meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的会议上开始打瞌睡了。
words.en: To fall into a light sleep, especially unintentionally.

words.tr: phrase. 假使；如果；万一；以防
words.ex: Keep a flashlight in case of power outage.
words.ex_cn: 以防停电，准备一个手电筒。
words.en: used to describe what should be done if a particular situation, especially a bad one, occurs

words.ex: In the long run, eating healthy saves money on doctor visits.
words.ex_cn: 从长远来看，健康饮食可以节省看医生的费用。
words.en: Over an extended period of time; in the future, especially in the distant future.

words.ex: Many people look on him as a hero.
words.ex_cn: 许多人把他看作英雄。
words.en: To consider or regard someone or something in a particular way.

words.ex: I look up the word in the dictionary.
words.ex_cn: 我在字典里查这个词。
words.en: If you look up a fact or a piece of information, you find it by looking in something such as a reference book or a list.

words.ex: He exercises on a daily basis.
words.ex_cn: 他每天锻炼。
words.en: If something happens on a daily basis, it happens every day.

words.tr: phrase. 每周一次地；按周地
words.ex: He exercises on a weekly basis.
words.ex_cn: 他每周锻炼一次。
words.en: If something happens on a weekly basis, it happens once a week or every week.

words.ex: The company conducts an audit on a yearly basis.
words.ex_cn: 公司每年进行一次审计。
words.en: Happening or done once every year.

words.ex: We must take the weather into consideration before planning the trip.
words.ex_cn: 在计划旅行之前，我们必须把天气考虑进去。
words.en: To think about and include something when making a decision or judgment.

words.tr: phrase. 算出；解决；锻炼；进展（顺利）
words.ex: I can work out the answer with a calculator.
words.ex_cn: 我可以用计算器算出答案。
words.en: If you work out a solution to a problem or mystery, you think about it and find a solution. If you work out the answer to a mathematical problem, you calculate it. If a plan or situation works out, it happens or progresses in a particular way.

words.tr: n. 酒吧间男招待员; 酒吧店主
words.ex: The barman served us a round of drinks.
words.ex_cn: 酒吧招待员给我们上了几杯酒。
words.en: A barman is a man who serves drinks in a bar.

words.tr:
v. 敢说；
n. 打赌；赌注；
words.ex: I bet you didn't know that.
words.ex_cn: 我敢说你不知道那件事。
words.en: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: The cafe attracts a young clientele.
words.ex_cn: 这家咖啡馆吸引了一群年轻的顾客。
words.en: The clientele of a business or organization are its customers or clients.

words.ex: He used cocaine last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚用了可卡因。
words.en: A drug obtained from the leaves of the coca plant, used as a local anesthetic and also illegally as a stimulant.

words.ex: The gambler lost all his money at the casino.
words.ex_cn: 这个赌徒在赌场输掉了所有的钱。
words.en: A gambler is someone who often gambles, especially someone who often risks losing money in the hope of winning more.

words.ex: He became addicted to heroin last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年对海洛因上瘾了。
words.en: Heroin is a highly addictive drug derived from morphine, which is itself obtained from the opium poppy. It is used illicitly for its euphoric effects.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: Mister Brown is my teacher.
words.ex_cn: 布朗先生是我的老师。
words.en: A title used before a man's name or position to address or refer to him politely.

words.ex: He drank coffee from a large mug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个大杯子里喝咖啡。
words.en: A mug is a large, deep cup with straight sides and a handle, used for hot drinks. It can also refer to someone's face or a foolish person. As a verb, it means to attack and rob someone violently in a public place.

words.ex: The mugger attacked him in the dimly lit alley.
words.ex_cn: 抢劫犯在昏暗的小巷里袭击了他。
words.en: A mugger is a person who attacks someone violently in a public place in order to steal their money.

words.tr: n. 毒贩；推进器；推进式飞机；（非正式）野心勃勃的人
words.ex: The police arrested a notorious drug pusher.
words.ex_cn: 警方逮捕了一名臭名昭著的毒贩。
words.en: A pusher is someone who tries to make other people do something, especially by persuading them in a determined way. In a negative sense, it can also refer to someone who sells illegal drugs.

words.ex: He spoke respectfully to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他恭敬地对老师说话。
words.en: In a way that shows respect or deference.

words.tr: n. 演艺圈，娱乐性行业
words.ex: He left showbiz to start a family.
words.ex_cn: 他离开演艺圈开始组建家庭。
words.en: The entertainment industry, especially the part of it that is concerned with popular entertainment such as music, films, and television.

words.tr:
n. 东西；原料；
v. 塞；填充；
words.ex: I need to clean up all this stuff.
words.ex_cn: 我需要清理这些东西。
words.en: If you stuff something somewhere, you push it there quickly and roughly. If you stuff a container or space with something, you fill it completely with that thing.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.ex: He sells his wares at the market every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都在市场上卖他的商品。
words.en: Goods or merchandise that are for sale.

chapters.name: Unit 3 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 加油；快点；拜托；来吧；开始
words.ex: Come on, you can finish this race!
words.ex_cn: 加油，你能跑完这场比赛的！
words.en: Used to encourage someone to do something or to hurry up, or to express disbelief or skepticism.

words.tr: phrase. 放开；松手；释放；放弃
words.ex: You need to let go of the past and move forward.
words.ex_cn: 你需要放下过去，继续前进。
words.en: To release or stop holding something or someone.

words.ex: He stopped talking abruptly.
words.ex_cn: 他突然停止了说话。
words.en: Suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.tr: adj. 注意的；专心的；留心的；关心的
words.ex: The child is attentive in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子上课很专心。
words.en: If you are attentive, you are paying close attention to what is being said or done.

words.ex: The bang woke me up at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 那声巨响在午夜把我吵醒了。
words.en: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion.

words.tr: n. 条状物；酒吧；栅栏；棒；
words.ex: He ate a chocolate bar after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一条巧克力。
words.en: A bar is a place where alcoholic drinks are served, or a long, narrow piece of metal or wood used for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
adj. 浅色头发的；金色的；白皙的
n. 金发女郎
words.ex: The blonde girl is singing in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那个金发女孩正在公园里唱歌。
words.en: A blonde person has hair that is pale gold in color.

words.ex: He put the suitcase in the boot of the car.
words.ex_cn: 他把行李箱放进了汽车的后备箱里。
words.en: A boot is a type of shoe that covers the whole foot and the lower part of the leg. It can also mean to kick something forcefully or to start a computer.

words.ex: He ran so fast that he became breathless.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得太快，结果气喘吁吁。
words.en: If you are breathless, you have difficulty in breathing properly, for example because you have been running or because you are afraid or excited.

words.tr:
n. 深褐色头发的白人女子；黑发女子
adj. （头发等）黑色的或深褐色的
words.ex: The brunette girl smiled at me.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑发女孩对我笑了。
words.en: A brunette is a woman or girl with dark brown hair.

words.tr: n. 旁观者；看热闹的人；局外人
words.ex: The bystander watched the accident but did not help.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者看着这起事故，但没有帮忙。
words.en: A bystander is a person who is present at an event or incident but does not take part.

words.tr:
v. 剧烈搅动；（使）猛烈翻腾
n. 搅乳器
words.ex: The machine churns the butter in the cream.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器剧烈搅动奶油来制作黄油。
words.en: To churn means to stir or shake milk or cream in order to make butter, or to move something around violently in water or air.

words.ex: The scientist created a cocktail of chemicals for the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 科学家为实验配制了一种化学混合物。
words.en: A cocktail is a mixed drink typically made with a combination of alcoholic beverages and other ingredients such as fruit juices, syrups, or cream.

words.ex: The car crash was a serious collision.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次严重的碰撞。
words.en: A collision occurs when two or more objects come into contact with each other, often resulting in damage or a change in direction.

words.ex: The currency in Japan is the yen.
words.ex_cn: 日本的货币是日元。
words.en: The system of money in general use in a particular country.

words.tr:
adj. 该死的；可恶的；糟透的
v. 咒骂（某人下地狱）
words.ex: It's a damn good idea.
words.ex_cn: 这是个该死的好主意。
words.en: If you say that someone is damned if they do something, you mean that they will be in a very difficult situation if they do it.

words.ex: He gave a deceitful smile to hide his lie.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个虚伪的微笑来掩盖他的谎言。
words.en: If you say that someone is deceitful, you mean that they behave in a dishonest way by making other people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: The magazine has a glossy cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本杂志有一个光滑的封面。
words.en: Something that is glossy is smooth and shiny.

words.ex: He grimaced when he tasted the bitter medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他喝下苦涩的药时皱起了脸。
words.en: A grimace is an ugly, twisted expression on a person's face, usually because they are experiencing pain or strong feelings.

words.ex: The children played in the grit near the road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在路边的沙砾中玩耍。
words.en: Grit is very small pieces of stone. It is often used to make surfaces less slippery. Grit is also a quality of character that enables someone to continue with determination in the face of difficulties.

words.ex: I could hear my heartbeat after running.
words.ex_cn: 跑步后我听到了自己的心跳。
words.en: The regular movement or sound made by the heart as it pumps blood around the body.

words.ex: The police used fingerprint identification to find the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用指纹识别来找到嫌疑人。
words.en: Identification is the act of recognizing and naming someone or something, or the process of proving who or what someone or something is.

words.ex: He showed his identity card to enter the building.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了身份证以进入大楼。
